afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 261020
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
320 AM MST Thu Nov 26 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry and tranquil weather will persist through at least the 
  weekend as temperatures gradually warm into a slightly above 
  normal range. 

- A Pacific low is likely to track through the Southwest United 
  States during the middle of next week, leading to a period with 
  gusty winds, rain chances, and cooler temperatures. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Early morning water vapor satellite imagery shows an innocuous upper 
low approximately over the Baja Peninsula, which led to the thick 
cirrus decks that tracked across the region Wednesday. Ensembles 
remain in excellent agreement that this feature will continue to 
meander south and east, eventually passing into Mexico this weekend. 
Meanwhile, the departure of the low will allow regional pressure 
gradients to slowly relax. Anticipate some lingering breeziness in 
Southeast CA, along the CO River Valley, and over portions of the AZ 
high terrain east of Phoenix today. Winds should then relax 
considerably Friday into early this weekend.

A couple more prominent features in satellite imagery this morning 
are a Pacific trough just north of Hawaii and second upper low 
centered off the British Columbia Coast, connected by a notably 
strong zonal jet streak. In fact, NAEFS mean 200 mb wind speeds are 
in excess of the 99th percentile of climatology, around 140 kts, as 
the jet punches onshore along the Oregon/Washington Coast. These 
features will progress further eastward, bringing positive midlevel 
height anomalies and broad anticyclonic flow over the region. Under 
anticylonic flow and positive midlevel height anomalies, 
ensembles show lower level thermal profiles warming, with 850 mb 
temperatures peaking around the 97th-99th percentile of 
climatology (19C-20C) across the western deserts and closer to the
92nd-95th percentile over Phoenix (17C-18C) on Friday. Despite 
the unusually warm temperatures aloft, forecast highs generally do
not exceed 5-8F above normal over the next few days. Instead, 
lower desert highs will peak mostly in the middle to upper 70s, 
and perhaps around 80F for some of the typically warmer spots out 
west. One complicating factor will be the influence of cloud 
cover, as GFS bufr soundings do indicate the introduction of thick
high clouds, moving in from the northwest this weekend. These 
clouds will help moderate surface temperatures during the day, 
preventing highs from warming further.

&&

.LONG TERM /SUNDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...    
By Sunday, anticyclonic flow aloft will transition to quasi-zonal as 
the upper low originally off the British Columbia Coast digs 
southeastward into the Central CONUS and remnant energy from the 
trough originally near Hawaii quickly ejects eastward through the 
Southwest US. Despite decreasing midlevel heights, lower level 
thermal profiles are not expected to respond strongly, and so lower 
deserts highs should continue to maintain at least the middle 70s 
through early next week. 

Ensembles are starting to come into better agreement with respect to 
a more significant Pacific low developing offshore the CA Coast
early next week and then tracking a cold front through the region
during the Tuesday-Wednesday timeframe. There are still 
considerable discrepancies in timing and the exact trajectory of 
this low, however, a few things are becoming more certain. H5 
heights aloft at the center of this Pacific low will deepen 
offshore early next week, with NAEFS mean values drop below the 
1st percentile of climatology. The Pacific low will displace 
downstream shortwave ridging further east as it nears the region, 
resulting in considerable height packing overhead. This setup will
support a strong, cyclonically curved jet streak which will 
attend the low as it progresses through the region. Strong 
regional pressure and temperature gradients ahead of the low 
(especially ahead of the cold front) will lead to a period of 
widespread gusty winds with speeds likely peaking in the afternoon
Tuesday as mixing taps the higher momentum air aloft. Moisture 
will also increase, although the extent of moisture return will 
depend on how far south the Pacific low digs. Strong southwesterly
flow aloft will likely result in IVT values surging in excess of 
the 90th percentile of climatology, around 250-350 kg/(ms). 
However, this will be relatively short lived due to the fast- 
moving, progressive nature of this system, and the best moisture 
will be confined ahead of the front. A brief period with moist 
isentropic ascent, modest WAA, and frontogenetic forcing could 
result in at least one band of showers with possibly some embedded
T-storms. Model uncertainty at this lead time is still too great 
to pin down any of these details. It is still conceivable this 
system passes mostly north of the forecast area, and the southern 
extent of a mostly dry cold front brushes the lower deserts during
the middle of next week. Regardless, as is typical with systems
like this, the Central AZ high terrain to the north and east of
Phoenix is favored to receive the better rainfall totals. Rain
shadowing effects over Southeast CA and far Southwest AZ will also
likely play a significant role in limiting rainfall totals. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0505Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
Uncertainty and high variability in wind direction will be the main 
weather issues through Thursday night as cirrus cigs gradually 
clear.  Confidence is good that an E/NE wind component will prevail 
the majority of the period, however, large variability will be 
common at times. At KPHX, the typical cold season counter-intuitive 
light SW component experienced the past few mornings may occur again 
early Thursday. In addition, there are slightly higher odds wind 
directions turn W/NW late Thursday afternoon/evening before 
reverting back to E/NE mid/late evening. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No weather issues will exist through Thursday night as cirrus decks 
gradually clear. Confidence is very good that winds will behave 
similarly to the past 24 hours, generally varying between a westerly 
and northerly trajectory. Extended periods of variability to nearly 
calm conditions will be common. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER... 
Dry and generally tranquil conditions will prevail through the
beginning of next week. Temperatures will be fairly stable through
the weekend in a 3F-9F above normal range. Afternoon minimum
humidities will vary between 15-25% areawide following fair to
good overnight recoveries between 30-60% through the weekend.
Humidity will then improve through the middle of next week. A
weather system will result in increasing southerly to 
southwesterly winds, especially by Tuesday, and increased chances
for wetting rain and possibly some isolated/embedded 
thunderstorms. Until then, anticipate winds to be light, mostly
below 15 mph, and only marginal breeziness over Arizona high
terrain and in the vicinity of the Lower Colorado River Valley
today.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...Updated 11/25 2040Z. 
Gila River: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area due to continued water releases upwards of 
2500 cfs. Water levels near Dateland continue to rise, with gauge 
data now showing a depth of just above 7.5 ft and flow around 1250 
cfs. At the current rate of rise, the water level at the Dateland 
gauge is expected to reach action stage (8 ft) by Friday. A separate 
Flood Warning segment remains in effect from Dateland to Yuma. These 
water levels will have the potential to flood farm fields and low 
water crossings along the river downstream from the dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Whittock
LONG TERM...Whittock
AVIATION...18
FIRE WEATHER...Whittock/Berislavich 
HYDROLOGY...Berislavich/Benedict/RW
